A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gradient-masking study. All 17 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet, alongside attack-radius experiments and appendix gradient-tracing results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a skip-connection ablation and transferability experiments in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The DnCNN front end, skip connection, frozen backbone, adversarial objective, very small learning rate, short training, and randomized model selection are retained. The additional architecture variants and skip-removal experiment evaluate the existing approach rather than replace its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate L-infinity adversarial image classification on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet. Appendix A.1 explicitly reuses the main experiments' subsets; its additions vary model configurations and attack procedures within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds comparisons between self-attacks, individual ResNet/ViT transfer sources, and ResNet-only, ViT-only, and mixed source ensembles, including leave-one-out and all-inclusive variants. These substantially expand the evaluated attack comparisons beyond the retained PGD, AutoAttack, BPDA, and front-end-bypassing transfer attacks.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings remain unchanged, but Appendix A.1 introduces systematic source-target comparisons across five ResNet and five ViT architectures, target-exclusion controls, and model-family aggregation. A second protocol compares seven CIFAR10 architectures across clean training and three adversarial-training strengths using 50-step PGD.

E4.justification: v2 adds a ResNet-18/CIFAR10 skip-connection ablation, qualitative learning-rate and training-duration sensitivity findings, and extensive transferability analyses across architectures, ensemble sources, and training strengths. The original attack-radius sweep, diverse-ensemble experiment, and gradient tracing are retained.

E5.justification: Matched results retain the same sample-based 99% confidence intervals, intermediate-result omissions, and zero-variance caveat. No new seeds, repeated-run counts, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are specified. The new transferability tables provide point estimates without additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original experimental table values are retained, but Tables 8-9 add extensive transfer results; for example, all-model-source attacks leave ImageNet mean accuracies of 18.1% for ResNets and 26.1% for ViTs. Table 2 also updates the external CIFAR10 extra-data clean/robust reference scores from 93.3%/71.1% to 93.7%/73.7%.

T1.justification: v2 introduces an ensemble-accuracy analysis with selection probabilities, attacker source minimization, Equation 7, and conditional accuracy calculations in Tables 5 and 7. This adds a substantive mathematical argument absent from v1. Equation 6 also corrects the second finite-difference evaluation from x_i + alpha to x_i - alpha.

C1.justification: The central claims about extreme gradient masking, misleading AutoAttack robustness, and the importance of adaptive attacks remain. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add a secondary contribution: examining whether randomized ensembling could provide a practical defense.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation of randomized defenses, including source-ensemble attacks, querying costs, and low mutual transferability as a prerequisite for usefulness. It also adds explanations of the skip connection's residual role, training sensitivity, and why large perturbations can change class semantics.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 documents PGD budgets and radii, source-ensemble construction, model-size variation, and reused evaluation subsets. Retained ViT labels now identify base models with 16-by-16 patches. These improve technical specificity, while the code-access information remains equivalent.

R1.justification: Section 2 gains a substantial treatment of moving-target defenses, randomized smoothing, ensemble transferability, and self-ensembling. Added works include Sengupta et al., Cohen et al., Bui et al., Bai et al., and Sitawarin et al., with substantive discussion of their assumptions and relationship to the new analysis.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract, copyedits retained prose, expands several explanations, renames Section 4 to Models and Attacks, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgments. The main section sequence and much existing prose remain intact; scientific additions account for most of the expansion.

P2.justification: v2 adds two transfer-result tables and two boxed assumption/calculation displays. It also changes Figure 2 to a text-wrapped placement and rearranges existing tables. The original figures retain their content, and v1 appendix Tables 6-8 become v2 Tables 10-12.

improvement.justification: The skip-connection ablation, transferability controls, expanded research context, and corrected Equation 6 improve evidence and clarity while preserving the central findings. However, Table 5 treats Table 8's family-averaged accuracies as bounds for individual model pairs, so the claimed accuracy guarantee above 54% is not established by the displayed evidence. This limits the benefit of the new practical-defense argument.
